page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 64-bit ARM (arm64) AWS Graviton processors. The bare-metal design grants direct access to the underlying hardware without virtualization hypervisor overhead. Compute resources consist of 96 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. With one thread per core, the system guarantees 96 dedicated vCPUs free from thread contention or shared virtual environment latency.

Memory capacity is configured at 192.0 GB, delivering a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local solid-state drives, necessitating external network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for storage requirements. Network interface capacity is substantial, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps to support heavy data transfers.

Hardware tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of discrete GPUs, shifting the server's architectural efficiency toward high-density CPU throughput and network data transport. The instance provides cost efficiency for scale-out workloads running on ARM-native binaries. Workload profiles that align with this hardware profile include network function virtualization, traffic inspection appliances, high-throughput microservices, distributed batch processing, and continuous integration compilation pipelines.
